post.caption: Bloodstone is green with red spots. It is dark green chalcedony, flecked with red spots of iron oxide. The name comes from the red spots, which look like blood. Its other name is heliotrope, Greek for sun turner. Ancient writers said it showed a red sun in a water bowl. Roman engravers carved it into signet ring stones. A design cut into the stone is called an intaglio. Bloodstone measures about 6.5 to 7 on the Mohs scale. Most bloodstone sold today comes from India. Brazil and Australia are other sources. It is one of March's two birthstones, next to aquamarine.
